keyFindings.description: The model round 6 retired is corrected in two places and still taught in six, and the body says both statements were corrected. staleRoomRetryBackoffMax's own comment now says the right thing - the ping does not depend on the ceiling, and no ceiling here could carry it - and forty lines below it armRetry, the constant's only caller and the place a maintainer stands when re-tuning or deleting it, still says the backoff climbs 'to a ceiling past the listener's idle period, which hands the wait back to the listener so its ping can prove the connection'. woke still ends 'the listener still gets its idle period back'. The backoff row's own premise still says the listener's wait is the sooner of the caller's wake and its idle period and that every wait ends at a wake so the ping never runs, and its Fatalf - the message a future maintainer reads when that row goes red - says waitFor returns that wake on every round so the ping never fires. In pglisten's own test, 'a wait the wake ended is not pinged' is contradicted by the row fifty lines below it. No runtime behaviour is affected and no code change is asked for: the remedy is six sentences and one body line. It is blocking for the reason this pull request has blocked twice before on the same class - round 4's enumeration and round 6's ceiling comment - and because these are precisely the sentences that would license removing the listener-side mechanism in the belief that the evictor's ceiling carries it.

Two stale facts. 'Proven by: ... seven rows' predates rounds 9 and 10: cmd/dispatch/multiprocess_test.go holds nine build-tagged Test functions, the two deferred-re-examination rows the body itself discusses among them, so the line understates its own evidence. 'Size: 73 files changed, +9,123/-883' does not match the branch at this head, measured at 74 files, +10,013/-1,353 over the whole diff and 70 / +9,428 / -1,353 excluding .legion/; the deletion figure is out by 470.

Two hardening items carried rather than demanded. The new row's 'wakes < 2' floor is load-sensitive in the opposite direction from its own ten-idle-period budget: a single 80 ms wake delayed past about 140 ms before the 300 ms ping turns a correct listener red, where a floor of one, or counting wakes after the ping, keeps the discrimination without the flake. And listenerPoolSize = 1 now backs three permanent listeners, so one listener's redial serialises behind another's dial, which pgxpool floors at a two-minute connect timeout; it costs reconnection latency only, since each hijack frees the slot at once, but the constant's comment still reasons about a single caller.

whatThisRoundProved.pingInvariant: traced at this head and not broken: every wait is capped at proven+idle through waitFor's untilPing; the only continue that skips the due-check is the notification path, which re-stamps proven two lines earlier; an untilPing at or below zero makes an already-done context that pgx answers without touching the socket, so the ping runs on the same connection and the ping re-stamps proven, so there is no spin; a wake asked at one nanosecond every round still lets time.Since(proven) climb to the boundary; proven moves only on a real round trip, so there is no premature ping, no extra dial and no redial loop; and both hookless callers take the NextWake == nil || OnWake == nil branch and wait exactly as before
whatThisRoundProved.probeDrivenNotArgued: TestAListenerWokenShorterThanItsIdlePeriodIsStillPinged reads '-- ping' back from pg_stat_activity for the listener's own pid, which is a statement the server ran rather than a call the code made, with dials == 1 asserted so it is the connection the listener already had and at least two wakes asserted so the row is a listener taking its wake branch. The control is the implementer's two-step revert: with only the ping decision reverted the row stays green, because waitFor's cap alone ends the wait at the due point, and with both halves reverted it fails with the backend's last statement still the LISTEN text. The two halves cannot be tested apart, since the cap reads the guard's own stamp - which is why the comment on the separable half is the first finding above
whatThisRoundProved.testerMeasurement: the architect's discriminating row was a negative result, recorded as one: the cap and the guard share the stamp, so no build has one without the other, and the row was dropped rather than landed as a row that proves nothing
